subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which scale measures earthquake magnitude on a logarithmic scale, so each step is ten times greater in amplitude?
questions.explain: The Richter scale is logarithmic, so each whole number is a tenfold increase in measured amplitude.

questions.q: Effects of an earthquake are often worse in a LIC than a HIC mainly because:
options: LIC earthquakes are always higher magnitude
Buildings are less able to withstand shaking and emergency services are weaker
HICs sit further from plate margins
questions.explain: Poorer building quality and limited emergency resources increase impacts in LICs.

questions.q: At a destructive (convergent) margin where oceanic meets continental crust, the denser oceanic plate is:
questions.explain: The denser oceanic plate is subducted into the mantle beneath the lighter continental plate.

questions.q: The middle-latitude atmospheric circulation cell, between the Hadley and Polar cells, is the:
questions.explain: The Ferrel cell operates at mid-latitudes between the Hadley and Polar cells.

questions.q: A conservative (transform) plate margin is one where plates:
questions.explain: At conservative margins plates slide past each other, so crust is neither created nor destroyed.

questions.q: Tropical storms generally do NOT form right at the equator because:
options: The sea is too warm there
There is too little Coriolis effect to make them spin
questions.explain: The Coriolis effect is near zero at the equator, so storms cannot start spinning.

questions.q: An example of an extreme UK weather hazard is:
options: A tropical cyclone forming over Britain
Heavy snow, flooding and winter storms
questions.explain: The UK experiences hazards such as flooding, storms, heatwaves and heavy snow.

questions.q: The epicentre of an earthquake is:
options: The deepest point of the earthquake
The edge of the tectonic plate
The point on the surface directly above the focus
questions.explain: The epicentre is the point on the ground surface directly above the focus.

questions.q: Which is an example of MITIGATION of climate change rather than adaptation?
options: Switching to renewable energy to cut emissions
questions.explain: Mitigation reduces the causes (emissions); adaptation copes with the effects.

questions.q: The calm, clear centre of a tropical storm is called the:
questions.explain: The eye is the calm low-pressure centre, surrounded by the violent eyewall.

questions.q: Which of these is a SECONDARY effect of an earthquake?
options: Fires caused by ruptured gas pipes
questions.explain: Fires from broken gas lines occur after the shaking, making them a secondary effect.

questions.q: Convection currents that move tectonic plates occur in which layer?
questions.explain: Heat-driven convection currents in the semi-molten mantle drag the plates above.
